text: Elias was behind the counter when he noticed the book. Its pages were dog-eared. The industrial ovens hummed, filling the air with the smell of yeast and burnt sugar. He wiped flour off his forearms and checked the clock, 3:17 AM, Thursday. The book, The Shadow of the Wind, was a worn paperback. It had been sitting on the glass display case for the past six weeks. He picked it up, feeling its familiar weight. Usually, he would just put it in the return bin behind the register, assuming someone had mistaken the late-night drop-box slot for a library return. But something felt different tonight. The book felt a bit warmer than the cool air of the shop. He opened it to the bookmarked page. A folded square of lined notebook paper dropped out and fluttered down to the counter. He hesitated, then unfolded it. The handwriting was jagged, hurried. It said, "I know you're reading it. Keep going. Page 204 changes everything." His heart hammered against his ribs, a sudden sharp rhythm that stood out against the quiet hum of the mixers. He looked around the empty shop, shadows stretching long across the tiled floor. No one was there. He looked back at the note, then at the book. With trembling fingers, he turned to page 204. The text blurred before his eyes. He closed the book, pressed it flat against the counter, and reached for his pen.
